record.name: Singapore AI Safety Institute
record.host: Digital Trust Centre at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), with IMDA
record.mandate: Conducts AI safety research, including testing and evaluation, and cooperates internationally.

funding.description: S$50m over five years from 1 October 2022 for the Digital Trust Centre
funding.notes: The source dates the establishment of the Digital Trust Centre to June 2022 and states initial funding of SGD 50m. NTU's page on the centre states that the SGD 50m grant from IMDA and the National Research Foundation started on 1 October 2022 and that they invested it over the next five years; the annual figure is the mean over five years counted from that start, and the founding year is not treated as a spending period. DTC itself was later designated Singapore AISI. The earlier allocation covered trust technologies, including AI testing and privacy-enhancing technologies; the source does not state an AI-safety allocation. This broader pre-designation funding remains related funding.
funding.annual_basis: Arithmetic mean of the SGD 50m grant over the five years NTU states, counted from the grant's start on 1 October 2022; annual disbursements are not stated. Related funding for the Digital Trust Centre before its designation, not the institute budget.

national_partners.notes: Cyber agency searched: Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA), 2026-10-19 (en); none found. Fetched: csa.gov.sg Cybersecurity Act page (200; no AISI mention), CSA about-us guess (404), CSA "Guidelines and Companion Guide on Securing AI Systems" page (200; no AISI/IMDA mention in the extract), sgaisi.sg home and about-us (no CSA named). No document naming cooperation between CSA and the Singapore AISI. The only body the sources name as a partner is the body the institute reports to, which is not an entry.

testing_capacity.notes: Joint network testing reported, 2025-06-26 (multilingual exercise) and 2025-07-17 (agentic exercise), and the bilateral agent data-leakage evaluation with Korea (2026). The testing is done by the Digital Trust Centre at NTU as the designated institute; IMDA is the policy partner.

model_access.notes: No access event, legal power or agreement providing for access to, or evaluation of, the models of a developer that has a model in Epoch AI's frontier set was found. The network pilot on Llama 3.1-405B (October to November 2024) used an open-weight model, which is public access, and the bilateral report with Korea used models available through public APIs. The IMDA-Microsoft MOU (12 June 2026) only explores a framework for structuring access to frontier models and is not an agreement with the institute. No legal power. In a written parliamentary answer of 6 October 2026, the ministry said it seeks access to frontier models where appropriate but does not make it a requirement.
